summary: Automated valuation is the sector's oldest deployed AI, and it is now formally regulated: federal quality-control standards for AVMs took effect in 2025. Valuation, leasing automation, 3D capture, and property operations are where AI actually runs; the regulator record and the platforms' own model documentation are the sources.

analysis.body:
Per the Census Bureau's Business Trends and Outlook Survey, 28.0% of firms in real estate and rental and leasing reported using AI in the latest measurement period, up from 25.6% in the prior period, making this one of the more measurably active sectors in the survey. The increase suggests continued diffusion rather than a plateau, though the figures cover the broad NAICS 53 category and do not distinguish between commercial and residential subsectors or between large platforms and small brokerages.

The most established AI application in the sector is automated valuation. Zillow publishes Zestimate valuations for more than 110 million homes using a neural network model that draws on county and tax assessor records, direct MLS feeds, and listing signals, with the company noting that its latest architecture incorporates expanded historical data to reduce overall error rates. HouseCanary covers more than 136 million U.S. properties with AI-powered valuations, forecasts, and analytics, combining machine learning with image recognition that identifies room types and assesses home condition from photos. Opendoor applies similar pricing models to make direct purchase offers to homeowners, an approach that ties balance-sheet capital directly to model accuracy. These platforms represent the consumer and institutional faces of the same underlying technology: algorithmic property valuation at scale.

That technology is now subject to binding federal rules. The FHFA, CFPB, OCC, Federal Reserve Board, FDIC, and NCUA jointly finalized quality control standards for automated valuation models used by mortgage originators and secondary market issuers in determining collateral worth. Under the rule, covered institutions must adopt policies and control systems to ensure a high level of confidence in AVM estimates, protect against data manipulation, avoid conflicts of interest, and conduct random sample testing and reviews. The CFPB's parallel work on algorithmic appraisal documents how valuation bias and model accountability are supervised on the consumer protection side. Together these rules mark the first time the sector's core AI has binding federal governance, and compliance obligations now attach to any lender relying on an AVM for a mortgage collateral determination.

Commercial real estate is automating a different set of workflows. JLL states that it has invested more in AI technology than any other real estate company, deploying it across brokerage, facilities management, and portfolio analytics. Building Engines, a JLL company, offers a property management platform whose Prism AI layer delivers answers, recommendations, and automation to help commercial teams reduce costs and grow net operating income. Prophia applies document AI to lease abstraction, extracting key terms and combining machine output with expert validation to produce structured lease data for owners and operators. EliseAI takes an agentic approach to leasing and resident communications, handling messages, calls, tour scheduling, prospect follow-up, and maintenance requests automatically around the clock. Matterport digitizes physical buildings into 3D models that support portfolio management, construction coordination via Procore and Autodesk integrations, and virtual tours intended to increase buyer and seller confidence and close transactions faster.

The organizational infrastructure around proptech is substantial. CREtech convenes what it describes as the world's premier real estate AI conference, bringing together owners, developers, investors, brokers, and technology leaders to share deployment strategies. The Center for Real Estate Technology and Innovation serves as a research and education organization for the proptech sector. NAR REACH, created by Second Century Ventures, operates as what it describes as the most active venture fund in global real estate technology, running a scale-up program for residential proptech companies. The National Association of Realtors tracks technology adoption across the profession, and the Building Owners and Managers Association covers AI applications in smart-building operations, energy efficiency, and predictive maintenance across commercial property types.

For a decision-maker evaluating deployment, the pattern across sources points to a sector where AI is no longer experimental in valuation, leasing automation, and document processing, but where regulatory complexity is rising in parallel. The AVM quality control rule means that any organization using algorithmic valuations in mortgage decisions faces mandatory governance requirements, not optional best practices. On the operational side, the ROI framing from vendors consistently centers on cost reduction and staff time freed for higher-value work, though the sources do not provide independently verified figures. The clearest near-term risk is model accuracy under changing market conditions, a concern Zillow itself acknowledges by noting that actual sale prices can vary due to negotiation and changing market conditions, and one that Opendoor has demonstrated carries real financial consequences when pricing models miss.
